claims.text: The deep neural network potential is trained on ab initio molecular-dynamics trajectories of representative high-entropy carbonitrides.
The neural network potential can predict melting temperatures across multiple TiZrTaHfNb carbonitride compositions.
The approach can predict enthalpy of fusion.
The approach can predict entropy of fusion and liquid-phase entropy.
The approach can determine the volume change at melting.
The neural-network-potential approach is computationally efficient relative to direct first-principles approaches.
The material scope includes crystalline TiZrTaHfNb carbonitrides with variable carbon and nitrogen content.
Heating/cooling hysteresis and two-phase coexistence molecular-dynamics methods can both be used to estimate melting.
The two-phase coexistence method operates under constant-pressure conditions.
Temperature sweeps cover superheated and supercooled regimes.
The training data encompass the range of bonding environments encountered throughout the claimed compositional space.
Changes in pair correlations and local coordination mediate the solid-to-liquid transition and composition-dependent melting behavior.
The neural network interpolates a high-dimensional potential-energy surface learned from ab initio data.
The potential captures both short-range interactions and long-range effects.
The learned potential enables simulation of nucleation events during melting.
Predicted melting temperatures will have errors of about ±30 K relative to experiment.
Enthalpy of fusion will show systematic composition-dependent trends associated with changes in chemical bonding and nitrogen content.
Entropy of fusion will show systematic nitrogen-dependent trends associated with local structure and chemical bonding.
Volume change at melting will show systematic composition-dependent trends associated with nitrogen content.
Reliability is expected to decline for compositions or thermodynamic conditions outside the bonding environments represented in training.
